Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

represent verb

portray in art

also portray, show (in a picture or statue), representation, a representation, express (in words), express

classical

Hor. AP 32–33
Plin. NH 34.66 (Lewis & Short)
M-O s.v. represent: imāginem exprimere
Traupman 29
Traupman 312

exprimō, exprimere, expressī, expressum

verb, third conjugation

represent, portray, model (in a statue or a picture)

Properly “press out”, and so “model” in wax, clay or bronze; Lewis & Short: in this sense mostly poetic and post-Augustan, frequent in the elder Pliny. Of a likeness: imāginem alicujus exprimere.

Other words

  • effingō, effingere, effīnxī, effictum — fashion, portray

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Verg. A. 6.32: cāsūs effingere in aurō; Cic. Div. 1.23 (Lewis & Short)

  • repraesentō, repraesentāre, repraesentāvī, repraesentātum — portray, represent (of painters and sculptors)

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Plin. NH 34.88 (Lewis & Short)

    Lewis & Short: in this sense post-Augustan. Not for acting on someone’s behalf (see represent, act or speak for).

Examples

  • Aemilium circā lūdum faber īmus et unguīs exprimet et mollīs imitābitur aere capillōs

    the humblest bronze-smith by the Aemilian school will render the nails and copy soft hair in bronzeHor. AP 32–33

  • bis cōnātus erat cāsūs effingere in aurō; bis patriae cecidēre manūs

    twice he had tried to portray the fall in gold; twice the father’s hands droppedVerg. A. 6.32–33

See also paint, picture, represent.
